Leave granted.
2. The appellants are aggrieved with the impugned judgment
of the High Court, which interfered with an order passed under
Section 203 of the Code of Criminal Procedure,  1973 (Cr.PC),
finding no  reason to  proceed with  the  complaint  filed  by  the
second  respondent  and  remanding  the  matter  for  fresh
consideration. The High Court noticed that the Court below failed
to  appreciate  the  injuries  on  the  de-facto  complainant,  the
appellant before it and rejected the complaint in an illegal and
mechanical manner without application of mind.
3. We heard the learned Counsel for the appellants and the
learned  Counsel  for  the  second  respondent  as  also  the
Government Advocate for the first respondent.
4. The  specific  case  of  the  appellant  was  that  he  was
Page 1 of 5
Crl.A @ SLP(Crl.) No.2608/2026

--- Page 229 ---
instrumental in raising a complaint against the Village Pradhan,
who was the brother of the de-facto complainant. The allegations
were misappropriation of funds in the development work carried
out in the village. The Village Pradhan, hence harboured enmity
against  the  appellant  and  through  his  brother  made  a  false
allegation  of  trespass  into  their  house,  assault  and  hurling
casteist  slurs  against  them;  the  appellants  belonging  to  the
Brahmin Community and the accused to the Scheduled Caste
Community.
5. The  complaint  filed  by  the  appellant  against  the  Village
Pradhan is produced as Annexure P1, which is dated 26.06.2023.
On 16.09.2023, a complaint was filed to the Superintendent of
Police and not informed to the Station House Officer of the Police
Station,  which  has  jurisdiction  over  the  area.  The  complaint
speaks  of  an  incident  of  15.09.2023  at  about  7  am  in  the
morning, where four people, the appellants herein, came to the
de-facto  complainant’s  house  and  perpetrated  criminal  acts
including the act of hurling casteist slurs.
6. Obviously, an enquiry was conducted pursuant to which the
appellants  also  had  filed  a  written  response  to  the
Superintendent  of  Police  as  seen  from  Annexure  P3.  The
appellants  pointed  out  that  individually  none  of  them  were
present in the locality on the particular day. Some documents
Page 2 of 5
Crl.A @ SLP(Crl.) No.2608/2026

--- Page 230 ---
were  also  produced  to  substantiate  this  contention.  The
concerned Circle Officer filed a report to the Superintendent of
Police  produced  along  with  Annexure  P4,  which  was  dated
13.10.2023  specifically  pointing  out  inconsistencies  in  the
statements made by the complainant as also the alleged victims
and  emphasized  that  none  of  the  villagers  spoke  of  such  an
incident having happened, when questioned.
7. The  appellant  then  filed  a  complaint  case  before  the
Additional District Judge SC/ST Act Jaunpur, which was registered
as Case No.36 of 2025. Similar allegations were made, which
were considered in detail by Annexure P7 order. PWs1 to 3 were
examined,  who  were  the  de-facto  complainant,  the  Village
Pradhan; the brother of the de-facto complainant and another
person as PW3, who is said to have witnessed the incident. There
were  stark  inconsistencies  in  the  narration  of the  incident  by
these three witnesses. As far as the injury on the complainant, it
was observed that the incident had occurred at 7 am and on the
same day and at 3.15 pm, a medical examination of the injured
was conducted. The Doctor opined that the injury caused was a
day old, hence, the injury could not have been caused from the
incident alleged. The Court also alertly pointed out that one of
the persons against whom allegations were raised, i.e. the 3 rd
appellant  herein,  was  not  present  in  the  locality  at  all,  as  is
Page 3 of 5
Crl.A @ SLP(Crl.) No.2608/2026

--- Page 231 ---
evident from a certificate issued from the inter-college in which

          UPON hearing the counsel the Court made the following
                             O R D E R
We  have  heard  Smt.  Rekha  Palli,  learned  senior
counsel/Amicus Curiae and Sri N.Venkataraman, learned ASG
appearing from the respondents.
From the affidavits filed on behalf of Ministry of
Finance and Ministry of Defence and as acknowledged by
learned Amicus, it is noted that pursuant to the directions
issued by this Court, the Ministry of Defence has extended
ECHS benefits to invalidated cadets and their medical
expenses through-out their life is taken care of. This is a
laudable measure.
It is also submitted by learned Amicus that the
monthly disability benefit, that is being paid to the
officer trainee (Army Cadet), + D.A. is Rs.12,240/- only,
whereas for a Jawan trainee/recruitee before attestation
(Army),  it  is  Rs.18,000/-  per  month;  that  there  is
disparity in the payment of ex gratia amount to out boarded
cadets.
2

--- Page 235 ---
In response to this submission, learned ASG drew our
attention to the fact that the Eighth Pay Commission has
been constituted and the said Pay Commission would consider
the enhancement in the rates of ex gratia payment that is
payable to the out-boarded cadets. In the circumstances,
liberty is reserved to the concerned persons to make their
representations and ventilate their grievances before the
Eighth  Pay  Commission.  We  think  that  the  Eighth  Pay
Commission would consider the matter from all aspects and
angles and accordingly may suitably enhance the ex gratia
payment being paid monthly to the out boarded cadets.
One other concern that was considered today was with
regard to the applicability of the Rights of Persons to the
Disabilities Act, 2016 to the out-boarded cadets. In that
regard, it was noted that the provisions of the said Act
may not be applicable to the cadets particularly those
whose bench mark disability is less than 40%. Therefore,
those  cadets  who  are  nevertheless  out-boarded  and  in
respect of whom the aforesaid Act does not apply, a
suitable scheme may be prepared and extended to them. 
Learned ASG submitted that he would seek instructions
on this aspect of the matter.
Insofar  as  Section  34  of  the  aforesaid  Act  is
concerned,  every  appropriate  government  has  to  make
reservation of not less than 4% of the total number of
vacancies in the cadre strength in each group of posts
meant  to  be  filled  with  persons  with  bench  mark
3

--- Page 236 ---
disabilities i.e., 40% and above. This is an aspect of
horizontal reservation. We find that the out boarded cadets
ought to be entitled to the benefit of the said provision
and make their applications for employment accordingly in
the reserved category in terms of the aforesaid Act. 
In this context, we place on record our appreciation
of those States which have considered the out boarded
cadets in the category of “ex-servicemen” for the purpose
of  employment  through  the  reserved  category.  This  is
another category of horizontal reservation.
The  States  are  directed  to  consider  granting
reservation to out boarded cadets in the quota of “Ex-
Military  Personnel  (Ex-MP)”  so  that  the  prospects  of
employment of these persons in the reserved category would
be enhanced in the States and Union Territories within the
respective cadres of posts in the services under the
States. 
For the aforesaid purpose the Registry of this Court
to dispatch a copy of this order to the Chief Secretaries
of the States for their consideration and implementation in
terms of Section 34 of the aforesaid Disabilities Act. The
said consideration shall be de hors the definition of “Ex-
Servicemen”  given  by  the  Department  of  Personnel  and
Training (DoPT) of the Central Government. 
We also direct that the respondent-Departments to
reconsider  the  recommendations  made  by  the  Sabharwal
Committee in its Report in light of the fact that the
4

--- Page 237 ---
matter is now taken up by this Court in order to ameliorate
the conditions of the out boarded cadets and we expect that
certain favourable recommendations would be emanating from
the respondent-Departments in this regard.
We also make it clear that the pendency of this
Petition before this Court would not come in the way of
Writ Petitions filed by individual persons seeking their
respective reliefs before the High Court being considered
on their own merits. In case those Petitions have been
disposed of on account of the pendency of this Suo moto
Writ Petition, liberty is reserved to those petitioners to
make an application seeking revival of their Writ Petitions
before the respective High Courts.

to reach to some understanding, the learned Mediator may
hear the applicants who propose to get themselves impleaded
in the present litigation before us. It will be within the
discretion of the learned Mediator in this regard.

shall be worked out in consultation with the parties.
Parties shall get in touch with the learned Mediator at the
earliest.

Mr. Justice S. Ravindra Bhat (Retd.) at the earliest.

          UPON hearing the counsel the Court made the following
                             O R D E R
1. For alleged violation of the order dated 19.01.2023 passed in LPA 425 of
2022, contempt proceedings have been initiated. The said order passed in the
LPA, is an offshoot of the challenge laid to a common order dated 04.08.2022
passed in WP(L) No.2535 of 2021, whereby a challenge was laid to the award
dated 04.07.2014 passed in Reference No.47 of 2007, under which the Central
Government  Industrial  Tribunal  (CGIT)  directed  the  petitioner  herein  not  to
remove  the  workers  and  to  regularize  the  110  workers  working  in  BSNL,
Daltonganj, Ranchi, 20-25 persons annually within a period of five years and the
said award came to be published on 17.02.2015.
2. For execution of the said award, there is already an execution petition filed in
MISC. Case  No.01/2021.  On  account  of  pendency  of  the  parent  SLP,  the
execution proceedings is said to have not been taken up. Hence, reserving
liberty  to the  said Executing Court to proceed in accordance  with law, the
present Special Leave Petitions are disposed of with following observation.
3.  We are making it explicitly clear that workmen, either by themselves or
through Union, cannot ride two boats at a time and the contempt proceedings
initiated in Contempt Petition No.928 of 2025  would not survive in view of the
execution proceedings already having been taken. Hence, reserving liberty to
the  workmen  to  proceed  with  the  execution  proceedings,  the  contempt
proceedings stands set aside or dropped. The execution proceedings shall be
expeditiously disposed of on merits.
4. Accordingly, the present Special Leave Petitions stand disposed of.
5. Pending application(s), if any, shall stand disposed of.
(RASHI GUPTA)                                   (AVGV RAMU)
COURT MASTER (SH)                             COURT MASTER (NSH)

IN THE SUPREME COURT OF INDIA
CRIMINAL APPELLATE JURISDICTION
CRIMINAL APPEAL NO.            OF 2026
(@SLP(CRL.) NO.9946 OF 2026)
P.  SATYANAGAMURTI & ANR. ..... APPELLANT(S)
              VERSUS
STATE OF CHHATTISGARH ..... RESPONDENT(S)
O R D E R
1. Heard.
2. Leave granted.
3. Appellants have been arraigned as Accused Nos.1 and 2 in connection
with FIR No.08/2025 registered for the offences punishable under Sections
318(4), 336, 317(4) and 3(5) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 (BNS)
and Section 66-D of the I.T. Act.
4. It is the case of the prosecution that de facto complainant was induced
through Instagram links and falls to invest in alleged Forex trading and
she had transferred Rs.48,67,500/- to various entities. Out of the said
amount,  Rs.15,00,000/-  was  transferred  to  the  account  of  “Parmar
T raders”.
5. Investigation revealed that mobile number linked to the said account
was registered in the name of Appellant No.1-Satyanagamurthi and as
such notice was issued and subsequently arrested on 29.11.2025 and
from  the  said  date,  they  are  in  custody.  After  completion  of  the
investigation, chargesheet has been filed.
1                                                                                    SLP(CRL.) NO.9946 OF 2026

--- Page 296 ---
6. Having heard the learned counsels appearing for the parties, we notice
that the chargesheet material prima facie does not indicate that the same
amount having been received to the account of the Appellant No.1. The
amount which has been transmitted to the account of Parmar T raders, was
linked  to  the  mobile  number  which  was  initially  said  to  have  been
registered in the name of Appellant No.1.
7. It is the case of the appellants that neither the prosecution nor the
complaint alleged that the appellants had induced the complainant. Only
on the basis of Sim Card link and its usage is relatable to the appellants.
The CDR details will have to be examined during the trial and prima facie
the entire evidence seems to be documentary or electronic in nature. It is
for the prosecution to link the accused for the such act. As such, we are of
the considered view that appellants are entitled to relief of bail. We also
make it clear that the opinion expressed by us is prima facie for the grant
of bail and same shall not influence the trial in any manner whatsoever.
8. Accordingly, appeal is allowed. Impugned order is set aside. Appellants
are ordered to be released on bail by the jurisdictional Court on such
terms  and  conditions  as  it  may  deem  fit  to  impose  and  also  on  the
condition that appellants would appear before the jurisdictional trial court
on all dates of hearing except when exempted for any specific reason.
2                                                                                    SLP(CRL.) NO.9946 OF 2026

--- Page 297 ---
9. Pending application(s), if any, shall stand disposed of.

(ARAVIND KUMAR)
..................J.
(VIPUL M. PANCHOLI)

          UPON hearing the counsel the Court made the following
                             O R D E R
1. Heard  Ms.  Vidhi  Pankaj  Thaker,  learned
counsel for the petitioners and Ms. Rukhmini Bobde,
learned counsel for the respondents.
2. The writ petitioners before the High Court
are the petitioners herein, who questioned the

--- Page 300 ---
2 SLP(C) No.  10310/2026
judgment dated 03.02.2026 passed by the High Court
in Writ Petition No. 2432 of 2023. The petitioners
filed the said Writ Petition questioning the Notice
dated 23.11.2022, issued by the first respondent,
calling upon the petitioners to remove the alleged
encroachment noticed by the Authorities.
3. We are not adverting to the rival claims of
the parties, vis-a-vis, the subject matter. One of
the grounds raised by the petitioners is that the
Notice dated 23.11.2022 has been issued without
giving an opportunity to determine the nature or
extent of encroachment by the petitioners.
4. In response to such a contention, in the
reply, the State has stated thus:-
“10. I further say that this Respondent
No.  1,  Office,  will  now  give  personal
hearing to the Petitioners, further after
following due process of Law and granting
fair  opportunity  of  hearing  to  the
Petitioners, will pass appropriate Order in
accordance with Law in the matter within
two months.”
5.  Ms. Vidhi Pankaj Thaker, argues that the
stand of the respondents could have been sufficient
to firstly allow the respondents to proceed in the
matter, however, by conforming to the requirements
of law and passing appropriate orders.
6. The impugned judgment, since it has not

--- Page 301 ---
3 SLP(C) No.  10310/2026
taken note of the stand of the respondents, there
is  a  possibility  of  the  respondents  ordering
demolition  without  following  the  procedure
contemplated under the Maharashtra Land Revenue
Code, 1966.
7.  Ms. Rukhmini Bobde, contends that what has
been  stated  before  this  Court  is  a  mere
apprehension. The respondents, having said, as has
been excerpted above, will not take the law into
their hands and demolish the structures.
8. We  have  heard  the  learned  counsel  and
perused the record.
9. In the circumstances of the case, we are of
the view that the order in Writ Petition No. 2432
of  2023  is  modified  by  observing  that  the
respondents are offered an opportunity, as has been
stated in the reply, within four weeks from today
to decide the matter and proceed to take possession
in accordance with law. The entire exercise is
completed within three months from today.
10. The petitioners are given two weeks’ time
from today to file their reply before the first
respondent.
11. The Special Leave Petition stands disposed
of with the above observations.
12. Pending application(s), if any, shall stand

--- Page 302 ---
4 SLP(C) No.  10310/2026
disposed of.

1. The unsuccessful defendant in Original Suit
No.1702 of 2024 is the petitioner.
2. The  suit  is  for  declaration  and  other

--- Page 308 ---
2
consequential reliefs. There is no dispute about
the relationship between the parties, except that
of the petitioner before us.
3. The petitioner moved the Trial Court under
Order 7 Rule XI of the Code of Civil Procedure,
19081 praying for rejection of the plaint. The
Trial Court dismissed the prayer, and the High
Court has confirmed the dismissal by the impugned
order. Hence, the Special Leave Petition.
4.  Mr. Huzefa Ahmadi, learned senior counsel
for the petitioner, has made two submissions on the
very plaint and also the nature of the prayer in
the suit. He argues that the suit is explicitly
barred by limitation and the prayer for rejecting
the plaint under Order 7 Rule XI CPC should have
been allowed.
5.  Ms.  Manisha  T.  Karia,  learned  senior
counsel for the respondent(s) contends that the
knowledge  now  attributed  to  the  plaintiff-
contesting respondent(s) is not from the correct
perspective. In the circumstances of the case, the
reason for moving the Court for the present reliefs
is stimulated from a suit filed by the legal
representatives of the brother(s) for partition and
other reliefs during and in the course of such
1 Hereinafter referred to as, ‘CPC’.

--- Page 309 ---
3
initiation, the knowledge has been derived by the
plaintiff. It is argued that these are matters of
trial and proof by way of evidence but not a simple
case for rejection under Order 7 Rule XI of the
CPC.
6. We have heard learned senior counsel for the
parties and perused the order(s) impugned.
7. The petitioner before us is aggrieved by the
rejection of the prayer under Order 7 Rule XI CPC.
Though a few submissions have been made, we are of
the view that these submissions are available to
the petitioner during and in the course of the
trial. Therefore, from the material at this stage,
we are not persuaded to express our view on the
points canvassed before us. After perusing the
order(s) impugned, we are of the view that it is
not a case of rejection of the plaint under Order 7
Rule XI CPC. We are in agreement with the view
taken by the High Court and the Trial Court, and we
dismiss the Special Leave Petition.
8. Accordingly,  the  Special  Leave  Petition
stands dismissed.
9. The dismissal of the Special Leave Petition
or, for that matter, the orders impugned, shall not
be understood as foreclosing the grounds available
to the petitioner for pressing during and in the

--- Page 310 ---
4

disposed of.

1. Leave granted.
2. By the impugned order, the appellant’s
prayer  for  suspension  of  sentence  was
rejected by the High Court. The appellant has
been  convicted  by  the  Trial  Court  for
committing offences under Sections 109, 302,
143 and 147 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860
and under Section 3(1)(r)(s) & 3(2)(v) of the
Scheduled  Castes  and  Scheduled  Tribes
(Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989.
3. While issuing notice to the respondent
on 29.05.2026, this Court observed that the
1

--- Page 316 ---
appellant (Accused No. 18) was the Sarpanch
at the time when the offence took place, and
even the wife of the deceased (PW-2) has not
ascribed  any  role  to  the  appellant,  of
assaulting the deceased.
4. Learned  counsel  for  the  respondent-
State of Telangana, opposes the prayer on
submission that the appellant has incited the
main  accused  who  actually  assaulted  the
deceased.
5. Considering  the  entire  facts  and
circumstances of the case, particularly the
role  ascribed  to  the  appellant  when  the
occurrence took place, we are inclined to
suspend  the  sentence  and  release  the
appellant on bail.
6. Accordingly, the impugned order is set
aside, and it is directed that pending appeal
before the High Court the appellant shall be
released on bail, subject to such terms and
conditions as may be imposed by the Trial
Court.
7. The observations made in this order
shall have no bearing on the merits of the
appeal, which shall be decided on its own
merits.

1. Leave granted.
2. The appellants challenge the judgment/order dated
18.02.2026 in Application U/s 528 BNS No.28385/2025 along
with Application U/s 528 BNS No.26149/2025 passed by the
High  Court  of  Judicature  at  Allahabad,  whereby  the
appellants’  applications  seeking  quashing  of  the
proceedings arising out of Crime Case (FIR) No.24 of 2024
of  Ahraura  Police  Station,  Mirzapur  District,  Uttar
Pradesh, for the offences punishable under Sections 419,
420, 467, 468, 471 and 120-B of the Indian Penal Code
were dismissed.

affidavit of compromise dated 01.08.2026 has been filed,
but the same is not on record. A copy thereof has been
handed over across the Bar. We have perused the same.
4. The contents thereof read as under:
“  1. We are parties to the above
proceedings.
2. That an FIR No.24 of 2004 dated
03.02.2024 under Sections 419, 420,
467,  468,  471  &  120-B  IPC  was
registered against the petitioners
1

--- Page 324 ---
by the Respondent No.2.
3. Now the parties have amicably
settled  all  disputes  voluntarily,
without coercion.
4. The informant has no objection to
quashing of the FIR, charge-sheet
and all consequential proceedings.
5. Continuation of proceedings would
serve no useful purpose.
6. This is a fit case for exercise
of powers under Article 142 of the
Constitution of India.
7.  The  parties  pray  that  this
Hon'ble Court take this compromise
on record and quash the criminal
proceedings. ”
5. Since the parties have amicably resolved all their
disputes, the continuation of criminal proceedings would
be an abuse of the process of law. In view of the same,
Crime Case (FIR) No.24 of 2024 of Ahraura Police Station,
Mirzapur District, Uttar Pradesh and all proceedings
arising out of it stand quashed and set aside.

O R D E R
1. Leave granted.
2. We have heard the learned counsel appearing for the
parties.
3. The  present  appeal  has  been  preferred  against
dismissal of an intra court appeal, preferred by the
appellants, challenging an order passed in a contempt
petition wherein the appellants were found guilty of
contempt.
4. The order passed in the Writ Petition by the High
Court  of  Jammu  &  Kashmir  and  Ladakh  was  only  for
consideration of the representation of the appellant, for
regularization.  The  same  has  been  considered  and
rejected. In view of the same, we do not find any willful
disobedience  involved.  The  only  remedy  open  to  the
respondent is to challenge the said order of rejection,
in the manner known to law.  
1

--- Page 357 ---
5. In our considered view, it is found that the High
Court has exceeded its contempt jurisdiction. 
6. In such view of the matter, we are inclined to set
aside the impugned order passed by the High Court dated
13.12.2024 as well as the order dated 26.07.2023 passed
in  CPSW  No.  98/2017.  Accordingly,  the  contempt
proceedings  shall  stand  closed.  However,  liberty  is
granted to the respondents to challenge the order of
rejection, in the manner known to law.
7. Accordingly, the Appeal stands allowed.
8. Pending application(s), if any, shall stand disposed
of.

                             O R D E R
We are not inclined to interfere with the
impugned order(s)/judgment(s) passed by the Division
Bench of the High Court. Accordingly, the Special Leave
1

--- Page 384 ---
SLP (C) No(s). 25921-25922/2026
Petition(s) shall stand dismissed.
At this stage, learned senior counsel appearing
for the petitioner prays for six months’ time to vacate
the premises.
It has been pointed out that the petitioner has
been in occupation of the premises since the year 2004
on a monthly rent of RS. 45,000/- (Rupees Forty Five
Thousand Only) and the rent has not been enhanced even
though the eviction proceedings were initiated in the
year 2009.
The  Learned  counsel  appearing  for  the
respondent-landlord opposes the prayer and submits that
the petitioner has been aware since the year 2009 that
he would be required to vacate the premises upon
initiation of the eviction proceedings. It is further
submitted that if time is granted by this Court, the
mesne profits ought to be enhanced with effect from the
date of the judgment of the Single Judge.
Considering the submissions advanced, we deem
it  appropriate  to  grant  six  months’  time  to  the
petitioner to vacate the premises, subject to the
following conditions:-
1. The petitioner shall file the usual undertaking
before this Court as well as before the High Court
within two weeks from today.
2

--- Page 385 ---
SLP (C) No(s). 25921-25922/2026
2. The petitioner shall pay mesne profits at the
rate of Rs. 2,00,000/- (Rupees Two Lakhs Only) per
month with effect from the date of the judgment of
the  Single  Judge.  The  arrears  not  only  of  the
decretal  amount  but  also  calculating  the  mesne
profit at the above rate from the date indicated
above till 31st January 2027 to be deposited within a
period of four weeks from today before the High
Court, which upon deposit shall be withdrawn by the
respondent(s).
3. In the event of default in complying with any
of the aforesaid conditions, the interim protection
granted  to  the  petitioner  shall  stand  vacated
automatically without any further reference to this
Court.

          UPON hearing the counsel the Court made the following
                             O R D E R
Learned counsel for the petitioner(s) submitted that the 
petitioners have undergone the sentence imposed by the Trial 
Court and which was affirmed by the High Court by the impugned
judgment. In the circumstances, consideration of this special 
leave petition is wholly academic.
However, the concern of the petitioners is regarding  
Order dated 26.10.2016 passed by this Court wherein this Court
has observed prima facie that the acquittal of the petitioners
contd..

--- Page 387 ---
- 2 -
under Section 306 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 (IPC) by the 
High Court may not have been as per law.  Hence, show  cause
notice  was  issued to the petitioners  as  to  why  the  
conviction under Section 306 of the IPC as recorded by the
Trial Court could not be sustained.  
For immediate reference, the said order is extracted as 
under - 
“The petitioner No.1 along with others was charged for
offences punishable under Sections 452, 354, 294, 504,
506, 323, 306 and 143 read with Section 149 of the
Indian  Penal  Code  (IPC),  1860.  The  Trial  Court
convicted  all  the  accused  persons  including  the
petitioner no.1 of all the aforesaid charges. However,
the High Court has acquitted the petitioner and few
others of the charges leveled under Sections 452 and
306 of the IPC. 
Prima facie, we are of the view that acquittal
under Section 306 of the IPC is not as per law.
Therefore, issue show cause 2 notice to the petitioner
as to why the conviction under Section 306 of the IPC
as recorded by the Trial Court is not sustained. 
Reply be filed by the petitioner within six
weeks.
Notice shall also be issued to the State of
Maharashtra, returnable in six weeks. 
Insofar as conviction for the offences upheld by
the High Court is concerned, against which the present
special leave petition is filed, no notice is issued
at this stage.” 
Learned counsel for the petitioners submitted that having
regard to the facts and circumstances of this case and
particularly bearing in mind that the High Court has acquitted
the  petitioners  under  Section  306  of  the  IPC  and  the
petitioners have already undergone the sentence under Sections
Contd..

--- Page 388 ---
- 3 -
451 and 354 of the IPC, we do not find any reason to consider
this special leave petition any furhter. 
In the circumstances, we do not find any reason to
proceed further in the special leave petition pursuant to
order dated 26.10.2016.
The special leave petition is according disposed having 
regard to the aforesaid discussion. 
Pending application(s) shall stand disposed of.

STATE OF HARYANA & ORS.         ...Respondents
O R D E R
1. Leave granted.
2. We have heard the learned counsel appearing for the
appellant  and  the  learned  A.A.G.  appearing  for  the
respondent-State.
3. It is agreed by the learned counsel for both the
parties that the issue involved in the instant appeal is
covered by the judgment of this Court in the case of
BESCO Ltd. v. State of Haryana & Ors.  reported in 2023
INSC  759,  wherein  the  compensation  awarded  to  the
landowners has been enhanced to Rs 1,49,14,975/- per acre
with standard statutory benefits.
4. In view of the above, the impugned order stands set
aside and the compensation payable to the appellant
stands  enhanced  to  Rs.  1,49,14,975/-  per  acre  with
standard statutory benefits. However, we make it clear
that for the period of delay of 662 days in filing the
1

--- Page 405 ---
appeal before us, the appellant shall not be entitled to
any interest. 
5. The appeal stands disposed of, accordingly.  
6. Pending application(s), if any, shall also stand
disposed of.

          UPON hearing the counsel the Court made the following
                             O R D E R
1. The  Special  Leave  Petition  arises  from
interlocutory proceedings. The grievance of the
petitioners  is  that  the  impugned  order
substantially decides the fate of the Suit as well,
and such a course is impermissible while disposing
of interlocutory applications. The amount paid to
the eligible parties towards compensation is lying
with the Court/National Highway Authority.
2. The learned counsel requests the Court to
continue to maintain the compensation in a Fixed
Deposit till the disposal of the Suit and direct
the Trial Court to complete the Suit expeditiously,
preferably within three months from today.
3.  Mr. Ankolekar Gurudatta, learned Advocate-
on-Record for the respondent No.1 submits that the
findings, at best, could be treated as having been
rendered  for  the  purpose  of  disposing  of  the
applications  and  that  the  petitioners,  if  are
successful, can certainly recover the amount from
the respondents in the Special Leave Petition.

--- Page 418 ---
3
4. We have heard the counsel for the parties
and taken note of the findings recorded by the
order impugned. It can be said that the findings
are intended only for the purpose of disposing of
the  application(s).  However,  to  clear  any
ambiguity, we make it clear that the Suit is
proceeded with and is disposed of on its own
merits, uninfluenced by the order(s) impugned in
the Special Leave Petition. The amount is lying
with the National Highway Authority for the benefit
of successful party. With a view to preserving the
subject-matter of the dispute. We direct that the
compensation be retained in the deposit till the
suit is disposed of. We direct the Trial Court to
dispose  of  the  Suit  expeditiously,  preferably
within six months from today.
5. Accordingly,  the  Special  Leave  Petition
stands disposed of with the above observations.
6. Pending application(s), if any, shall stand
disposed of.
(SNEHA DAS)                                 (NIDHI MATHUR)

office report dated 04.08.2026.

pending before the Court of VI Additional Principal Judge, 
Family Court, Chennai to the Court of Principal Judge,  
Family Court, Bengaluru, Karnataka.
3. The aforesaid case emanates from the petition filed by 
the  respondent-husband  under  Section  9  of  the  Hindu 
Marriage Act, 1955 seeking restitution of conjugal rights.
4. We have perused the grounds mentioned in the Transfer  
Petition and we are satisfied that a case has been made  
out for transfer of the proceedings.
5. Accordingly, we direct that the entire case record of  
O.P. No.20/2026 shall be forthwith transmitted from the  
Court of VI Additional Principal Judge, Family Court,

Bengaluru, Karnataka.

Dhanera, District-Banaskantha, Gujarat, for the offences
punishable under Sections 65-A, 65(e), 116-B, 98(2), 99, 81
and 83 of the Gujarat Prohibition Act, 1949 and Sections
465, 468 and 471 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860,
1

--- Page 672 ---
2. The  FIR  was  registered  on  28.12.2022,  and  the
petitioner was named in the FIR. Total 690 loose bottles of
IMFL was recovered.
3. The petitioner was absconding for almost two years,
which has resulted in a delay of investigation as well as
trial.
4. This Court, keeping in view the reply filed by the
respondent-State and especially keeping in view that the
petitioner was absconding for almost two years, does not
find any reason to allow the application for grant of
anticipatory bail. Accordingly, the Special Leave Petition
stands dismissed. However, the petitioner shall be free to
file a fresh application for grant of regular bail before
the Trial Court.
6. It is needless to observe that the observations made
in this order are confined only to the extent of grant of
anticipatory bail, and the Trial Court shall decide the
application for grant of regular bail uninfluenced by the
order passed by this Court, and on its own merits.
7. Pending application(s), if any, shall also stand
disposed of.

          UPON hearing the counsel the Court made the following
                             O R D E R
Delay condoned.
We have heard the learned counsel appearing for
the petitioner(s) and the learned Senior Counsel
appearing for the respondent(s).
Learned counsel appearing for the petitioner,
placing reliance on Section 46 of the Maharashtra
Tenancy and Agricultural Lands (Vidarbha Region)

--- Page 834 ---
2
Act, 1958 (hereinafter referred to as ‘the Act’),
submits that it overrides even Section 129(b) of the
Act.
However, we do not think so.
The earlier request made by the petitioner(s)
for fixation of the purchase price was rejected on
the basis of Section 129(b), which has become final.
We  are  dealing  with  a  case  where  the
registration of the Trust was in existence much
prior to the coming into force of the Act and the
findings of the authorities on the earlier occasion
which has become final between the parties is to the
effect that the respondent No.1 is entitled to the
benefit of Section 129(b) and the same is applicable
to the case of the parties.
In such view of the matter, we do not find any
error in the impugned order passed by the High Court
warranting interference.
The Special Leave Petition stands dismissed,
accordingly.
Pending  application(s),  if  any,  shall  stand
disposed of.

ITEM NO.39               COURT NO.10               SECTION XI-B
               S U P R E M E  C O U R T  O F  I N D I A
                       RECORD OF PROCEEDINGS
CONMT.PET.(C) Nos.219-220/2026 in C.A. Nos.11904-11905/2025
PUNNEN KURIAN                                         Petitioner(s)
                                VERSUS
MATHEW JOHON & ORS.              Respondent(s)/Alleged Contemnor(s)
 
Date : 05-08-2026 These petitions were called for hearing today.
CORAM : 
         HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE AHSANUDDIN AMANULLAH
         HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE MANMOHAN 
For Petitioner(s)  Mr. A. Raghunath, AoR                  
 
For Respondent(s)  Mr. P. V. Dinesh, Sr. Adv.
                   Ms. Anna Oommen, Adv.
                   Ms. Anne Mathew, AoR                            
          
                             O R D E R
Heard learned senior counsel/counsel for the parties.
2. The alleged contemnors/respondents are also present in the
Court. 
3. It is an admitted position that the order dated 17.09.2025
passed by this Court in C.A. Nos.11904-11905 of 2025 (Karukachal
Grama Panchayat  v. Punnen Kurian &  Ors. ) has not been complied
with. The same had to be complied with within two months from the
date of passing of the order, failing which the total amount
payable with regard to the area in question at the rate of
Rs.12,00,000/- (Rupees Twelve Lakhs) per cent had to be paid with
interest @14 per cent per annum to be recovered personally from the

--- Page 962 ---
2
persons who are responsible for the delay.
4. We further note that the learned senior counsel appearing for
the alleged contemnors/respondents had assured the Court that such
payment would be made within two months from that day.
5. Law is clear on the issue that once an undertaking/assurance
is given by a learned counsel on behalf of the client, the same is
considered to be binding on the client.
6. On this, we find that there is an ex-facie contempt of this
Court as the assurance has not been fulfilled.
7. Having regard to the aforesaid, as the alleged contemnors are
present in the Court, the Court is persuaded to frame charges for
contempt against the alleged contemnors/respondents. The Charge
would read as under:-
You are charged with wilful and deliberate disobedience and
non-compliance of the assurance given to this Court as recorded in
order dated 17.09.2025 in C.A. Nos.11904-11905 of 2025 (Karukachal
Grama Panchayat v. Punnen Kurian & Ors.).
8. The alleged contemnors/respondents shall be personally present
before the Court along with their show-cause on 06.10.2026, when
the matters be listed at the top of the Board.
9. However, by way of extra-ordinary indulgence, if the order
dated 17.09.2025 stands fully complied with before the next date of
listing and proof thereof is brought on record by way of an
affidavit, the Court may take a lenient view in the matters.
(SAPNA BISHT)                                   (ANJALI PANWAR)
COURT MASTER (SH)                             ASSISTANT  REGISTRAR

               S U P R E M E  C O U R T  O F  I N D I A
                       RECORD OF PROCEEDINGS
Transfer Petition (Criminal) No. 746/2026
NILESH JAIN                                        Petitioner(s)
                                VERSUS
SUNEETA KHANNA                                     Respondent(s)
(IA No. 208008/2026 - EX-PARTE STAY and IA No. 208009/2026 -
EXEMPTION FROM FILING O.T.)
 
Date : 03-08-2026 This matter was called on for hearing today.
CORAM : HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE SHEEL  NAGU
For Petitioner(s) : Miss Ritu Reniwal, AOR
                  
Mr. Naman Sherstra, Adv.
Mr. Siddharth Gontia, Adv.
Mr. Chirantan Saha, Adv.
 
For Respondent(s) : 
          UPON hearing the counsel the Court made the following
                             O R D E R
1. Learned counsel for the petitioner does not dispute that
except the ground of inconvenience, there is no other ground
available to the petitioner for seeking transfer of Criminal case
no. 60108 of 2024 titled, “Suneeta Khanna vs. Nilesh Jain” from the
Court of Ld. Chief Judicial Magistrate (VII), Lucknow, U.P. to the
Court of Ld. Chief Judicial Magistrate, Jabalpur, Madhya Pradesh.
2. The judgment of this Court passed by the Division Bench in
”M/s Shri Sendhur Agro & Oil Industries vs. Kotak Mahindra Bank
Ltd. in TP (Crl.) No. 608/2024 reported in 2025 INSC 328”  comes in
the way of the petitioner, the relevant portion of which is
reproduced below:”
“xxxx              xxxx xxxx
65.  For  the  purpose  of  transfer  of  any  case  or
proceedings under Section 406 of the Cr.P.C., the case
must fall within the ambit of the expression “expedient
for the ends of justice”. Mere inconvenience or hardship

--- Page 1008 ---
that the accused may have to face in travelling from
Coimbatore  to  Chandigarh  would  not  fall  within  the
expression “expedient for the ends of justice”. The case
must fall within any of the five situations as narrated
in para 49 of this judgment. It is always open for the
petitioner accused to pray for exemption from personal
appearance or request the Court that he may be permitted
to join the proceedings online.
xxxx              xxxx         xxxx”
 
3. In view of the above, no case is made out. Since the only
ground raised is inconvenience, the petition stands dismissed.
4. The Transfer Petition is accordingly dismissed.
5. Pending application(s), if any, shall stand disposed of.
(KANIKA TAYAL)                              (AJEET SINGH TARIYAL)
COURT MASTER (SH)                               BRANCH OFFICER

         HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE VIJAY BISHNOI
For Petitioner(s) : 
                   Mr. Amit Kumar Singh, AOR
                   Ms. K Enatoli Sema, Adv.
                   Ms. Chubalemla Chang, Adv.
                   Mr. Prang Newmai, Adv.
                   
                   
For Respondent(s) : 
          UPON hearing the counsel the Court made the following
                             O R D E R
1. Delay condoned.
2. The submission on behalf of the petitioner is that
death occurred after six years of the accident and,
therefore, the High Court committed manifest error in
computing compensation by treating it as a death claim
when it ought to have been treated as an injury claim.
3. We have gone through the records.  As per the
1

--- Page 1010 ---
records and the testimony of the doctor, it appears to
be a case where the injury had caused 100% disability,
as the person injured had to resign from his job.
4. In  such  circumstances,  the  ultimate  compensation
awarded is not on the higher side.  Therefore, while we
leave the question of law open for consideration in an
appropriate case, we decline to interfere with the
impugned judgment in exercise of our jurisdiction under
Article 136 of the Constitution of India. Accordingly,
the special leave petition is dismissed.
5. Pending application(s), if any, shall stand disposed
of.
  (KAVITA PAHUJA)                               (SAPNA BANSAL)
